description: List what happened in this workspace after the cursor you pass, oldest first. With no cursor it starts at the oldest event still kept. Events are kept 24 hours, so read at least that often. A webhook can be missed, but everything in that window is here. To read back from the newest event instead, pass `order: "desc"`. A cursor works only with the `types` and the `order` it came from. Each event's `seq` is the same number a webhook body carries as `seq`: match a callback to this list by `seq`, not by `id` (a webhook's `id` is the delivery's). Every page answers `generation`, which says which run of `seq` numbers it belongs to. After we restore from a backup the generation changes, and a cursor from an older one answers 409 `feedResetRequired` with `details.resetRequired: true`. Read again without a cursor, then check your mailboxes, sends and handoffs: a restore does not bring back an event it lost. A page read oldest first also answers `resumeCursor`, the place to pick up from: keep it once you have handled the page, and pass it as `cursor` next time, because `nextCursor` is null on a page that is not full. A key an owner limited to some mailboxes and agent inboxes sees only the events of those, and an event that names no mailbox is left out. While our team stops an address from receiving mail (`mailbox.review_changed` with `receiving: true`), its `message.received` events are left out. They come back when our team releases the address, unless they are older than the 24 hours we keep events. `tracking_domain.state_changed` reports a tracking domain whose DNS status or `inUse` changed: `{trackingDomainId, hostname, from, to, inUse}`. `from` and `to` can be equal when only target resolution or HTTPS proof changed. `inUse` is readiness after the change, not whether a campaign opted into tracking. Unanswered checks keep the last known state. Unchanged checks, adding and removing a domain fire nothing. Read `list_tracking_domains` for the current checks.

cursor.description: Where the last page stopped: the nextCursor of the answer before. Use it with the same filters it came with. Left out, the list starts at the beginning.

limit.description: How many to return in one page, 1 to 200. Left out, the server picks.

order.description: asc (the default): oldest first, the order to replay in. desc: newest first, to read what just happened. A cursor only works in the order it came from.

types.description: Only events of these types. In a URL, repeat the parameter: ?types=send.sent&types=send.failed.

name: list_events
title: List events
